How can I create AI product photos from a reference image with tested prompts and visible inputs and outputs? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
Creating high-quality AI product photos from a reference image requires a structured "Image-to-Image" workflow. Instead of letting the AI invent details, you anchor the generation using a clean, real-world photograph of your product and guide the surrounding environment using bounded, art-directed text prompts. 
nightjar.so
 +4
The step-by-step workflow, paired with tested prompts and a clear visualization of inputs and outputs, provides a repeatable blueprint.
1. Step-by-Step AI Product Photography Workflow
Prepare the Input Packet: Keep the original product SKU details, actual dimensions, and a high-resolution, unedited source photo together. 
www.gotolstoy.com
 +1
Clean the Reference Photo: Use an isolated product photo (ideally a 2048×2048 px PNG) on a crisp white or neutral gray background. Ensure the lighting is diffuse and flat, as harsh shadows will "bake" into the final AI environment. 
Figma
 +1
Select the Model & Adjust Settings: Upload the reference photo to an AI generator (such as Figma Weave, Nano Banana Pro, or LTX Studio). Set the Creativity/Image Weight Slider to a lower value (e.g., 20% to 40%). This forces the AI to keep the exact silhouette, packaging text, and brand logo untouched while changing only the background. 
PrompTessor
 +3
Write a Bounded Prompt: Describe the final scene's lighting, surface texture, and camera angle. Explicitly state what features must stay intact. 
Figma
 +2
Quality Assurance (QA): Generate multiple variations and compare the outputs directly against the original reference image. Inspect text legibility, seams, and brand colors before exporting. 
OpenArt
 +3
2. Tested Prompts, Inputs, and Outputs
The table below demonstrates how the inputs (Reference Image Features + Prompt) translate directly into specific outputs (Visual Elements) across common e-commerce categories.
E-commerce Category	Visible Input: Reference Requirements	Tested Text Prompt Template	Visible Output: Expected Result
Beauty & Skincare	• White backdrop
• Clear bottle label text
• Sharp 3/4 angle view	"Commercial hero product shot of the [SKU/Product Name] bottle resting on a wet, light beige travertine stone slab. Background features soft morning daylight and organic shadows of botanical monstera leaves. Photorealistic, crisp label text, shallow depth of field, 8k resolution, maintaining the exact bottle silhouette and font as the reference image."	• Legible 4-point type
• Wet stone texture reflection
• Dappled sun rays
• Accurate brand color
Luxury Accessories (e.g., Leather Bags)	• High-res PNG
• Visible hardware/buckles
• Sharp stitching lines	"Editorial lifestyle photography of the [Product Name]. The bag is placed on a minimalist pale concrete bench outdoors. Soft, overcast natural daylight. Vertical crop with ample copy space at the top. Preserve the original leather grain texture, handle stitching, and metallic logo precisely from the reference image."	• Realistic leather grain
• Clean canvas edges
• High-end commercial look
• Negative space for ad text
Home Goods & Decor	• Isolated furniture piece
• Even, diffuse lighting
• Complete product view	"Interior design catalog photo. The [Product Name] sofa positioned centrally in a bright, Scandinavian-style living room. Light oak wood floors, a large minimalist window showing a blurred garden backdrop, warm afternoon sun. Keep the exact fabric upholstery texture and dimensions of the sofa from the source photo."	• Photorealistic shadow underneath the sofa
• Cohesive room perspective
• Unaltered fabric color
3. Optimization and Repeatability
To scale this process into a permanent workflow for massive e-commerce catalogs:
Save Approved "Recipes": Once a prompt structure produces a flawless output, lock in the exact text prompt, model settings, and lighting keywords. 
nightjar.so
 +1
Batch Processing: Feed different product variants (SKUs) into the same prompt recipe to ensure visual consistency across an entire seasonal collection or online storefront. 
Designkit
 +1
Use Reverse Engineering: If you have a lifestyle photo whose style you want to replicate for a new product, run that image through an AI Image-to-Prompt tool to extract the exact keywords for lighting and art direction. 
Picsart
 +1
To help narrow down the best tool and settings, could you tell me:
What specific type of product are you photographing (e.g., cosmetics, electronics, apparel)?
Do you need marketplace-ready studio shots or lifestyle context photos?
Which AI generation platform do you currently plan on using?
